purpose: Test whether abstract task requirements can be separated from concrete capability providers, composed into a multi-step plan, and independently gated by availability and authority.

test_run.note: Tests were run against the same prototype and lab-manifest contents committed to the repository. This was not a GitHub Actions run and did not execute device capabilities.

sample_safe_composition.task: Inspect the manifest and reason about the task

sample_blocked_composition.task: Read a file, then write a copy

observations: The prototype can compose more than one abstract requirement without collapsing the task to a single required_capability.
Requirements and providers remain distinct: e.g. filesystem.read is not identical to read_file.
Authority is checked independently per step and blocked steps are not silently skipped.
UNSATISFIABLE remains an explicit output when no provider exists.
The experiment does not establish general natural-language decomposition; the v0.01 extractor is intentionally conservative and rule-based.
next_discriminating_test: Replace the rule-based semantic extractor with a replaceable non-China host or another independently testable decomposer that outputs abstract requirements only, while keeping discovery, composition, authority, and execution outside the host model.
